# Audition, freeze, and project workflow

## Audition a selection

Select one or more Score objects and choose **Project → Audition
ScoreObjects**, or press **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+A**. Blue renders a disposable
copy containing only the selected SoundObjects or audio clips, so the active
project is not rewritten and unrelated timeline items are excluded. The
audition starts at the earliest selected item's start and runs through the
latest selected item's end; an enabled mixer can extend the tail by its
extra render time. Interact with the Score timeline to stop auditioning.

## Freeze a ScoreObject

Save the project before freezing: Blue writes each freeze file beside the
`.blue` project. Select timeline SoundObjects (including FrozenSoundObjects
to unfreeze), then use **Freeze/Unfreeze ScoreObjects** in the context menu.
Freeze renders a SoundObject to audio and replaces it with a
FrozenSoundObject; unfreeze restores its nested source. Audio clips are not
freeze targets. If any selected item is unsupported or a freeze render fails,
Blue leaves the selection unchanged. The freeze dialog reports progress,
output, and any failure. Save the project again after success, and keep its
generated audio files with the project when moving it. Freeze uses the
project's instruments, tables, global code, and render settings, so fix any
Csound error before retrying. See [Rendering](rendering.qmd) for ordinary
disk output.

## Blue variables in Csound text

Blue substitutes the following tokens in the appropriate generated CSD
contexts. The Csound editor's **Blue Variables** menu inserts supported
tokens; inspect **Project → Generate CSD to Screen** to see actual values.

| Token                     | Meaning                                                                      |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<TOTAL_DUR>`             | Duration computed from the generated Score timeline; useful in Global Score. |
| `<PROCESSING_START>`      | Start used for always-on processing.                                         |
| `<RENDER_START>`          | Selected render start before absolute time conversion.                       |
| `<RENDER_START_ABSOLUTE>` | Render start after the Score's time conversion.                              |
| `<INSTR_ID>`              | Current instrument ID in supported instrument or note-template contexts.     |
| `<INSTR_NAME>`            | Current instrument name/ID without score quoting, for code identifiers.      |

`<TOTAL_DUR>` is calculated from timeline notes, not from extra events
typed into Global Score. A Global Score event can still lengthen the
actual Csound render. See [Globals](globals.qmd).

## Historical workflows

The older Java Blue manual describes an automatic minute-by-minute project
backup with a recovery prompt, a `blue --compile` command, and a Script
Library that runs Python against Blue's application object model. Those
workflows are not established in the current Blue 3 application. Save
projects explicitly, keep versioned copies when needed, and use the
current **Project → Generate CSD to File** command for a CSD export.
The **Python Console** is for the supported Jython session; it does not
replace the old Script Library's project-editing API.
